title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
quote: In Trace A, 80% of the reuse time falls within less than 10 minutes, while in Trace B it falls within 10 seconds.
proves: Alibaba Bailian (Qwen) production study: reuse is skewed (19% of user requests in trace A, 4% in B give >90% of block hits); single-turn requests give 97% of hits in API trace B; ideal infinite-cache hit rates 62%/54%; capacity of about 2x per-GPU HBM approaches ideal hit rate; workload-aware (WA) eviction gets 1.5-3.9% higher hit rate than best baseline and up to 41.4% mean response time gain vs LRU/LFU.
does_not_prove: Hit-rate gain over the best baseline is only a few points; no isolated LRU hit-rate number in text; datacenter scale and large models, not single-device; full trace not released (only a 2-hour sample, see B21).
bearing: supports: reuse is predictable per workload type; threatens: big hit-rate wins from fancier eviction (gain over best baseline is 1.5-3.9 pts)

title: When Fancy Eviction Fails: Rethinking Cache Replacement For LLM Prefix Reuse
quote: LRU is within 0.4 points of the best online algorithm on every trace
proves: 14 eviction algorithms (recency, frequency, learned) on two production traces (FreeInference 10.5B tokens, agent-heavy; Chutes 9.7B tokens) give little benefit over LRU because session pacing makes recency predictive; at 24 GiB on Qwen To-B trace S3-FIFO 0.491 vs LRU 0.403 hit ratio; by 1 TiB LRU within 0.4 pts of best; 84.9% of single-turn prompt blocks are accessed exactly once; block-level beats session-level eviction in HBM regime (session-level costs LRU 10.5 pts at 24 GiB); compute-aware partial-node eviction in vLLM cut TTFT 19.9% at 48 GiB; large gap to Belady remains.
does_not_prove: Datacenter GPU capacities (24 GiB+), not small unified memory; traces and simulator promised but not yet released; the small-capacity S3-FIFO win and compute-aware win are the open edges, not settled.
bearing: threatens: generic fancy eviction at large capacity; supports: one-hit quick demotion / admission and compute-aware partial eviction at small capacity (Mac 16 GB is exactly the small-capacity regime)

title: Learned Prefix Caching for Efficient LLM Inference (LPC)
quote: LPC achieves 18-47% reductions in required cache sizes for equivalent hit ratios
proves: Learned eviction that predicts from conversation content whether a conversation will continue, combined with last-access time, shrinks cache size needed for the same hit ratio by 18-47% on three real datasets; 11% prefill throughput gain.
does_not_prove: Throughput gain only in an emulated environment; abstract only (full paper not opened); predictor cost on-device not measured here.
bearing: threatens: learned/content-aware eviction as novel; supports: small-cache regime matters

title: Tail-Optimized Caching for LLM Inference
quote: achieves up to 27.5% reduction in P90 tail Time to First Token latency
proves: LRU ignores conversation length and can be arbitrarily bad for tail latency; Tail-Optimized LRU (small modification, provably optimal under a stochastic conversation model) cuts P90 TTFT up to 27.5%, P95 23.9%, SLO violations at 200 ms up to 38.9% on WildChat. Now shipped in SGLang as tlru (see B6).
does_not_prove: Simulated/stochastic-model evaluation on one dataset; mean TTFT effect not the target.
bearing: threatens: tail-aware eviction (already in SGLang); supports: measuring it on vLLM where it is absent

title: Not All Tokens Are Worth Caching: Learning Semantic-Aware Eviction for LLM Prefix Caches (SAECache)
quote: up to 756x variation in reuse rates
proves: Reuse rate differs by up to 756x across token types (system prompt, user query, chain-of-thought); multi-queue eviction with online-learned token weights gives 1.4x-2.7x TTFT over production-style baselines; fixed-parameter variants degrade up to 2.7x under workload mismatch.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; which baselines and capacities unclear; no single-device result.
bearing: threatens: token-type-aware eviction (e.g. evict thinking tokens first) as novel; supports: reasoning-token eviction gap on small devices

title: SGLang docs: Radix eviction policy
quote: The prefix unused for longest.
proves: SGLang exposes --radix-eviction-policy with lru (default), lfu, slru (protected_threshold, default 2), priority, tlru (threshold, next_prompt_estimate); fifo/mru/filo exist only for experiments; ties fall back to LRU; policy only ranks evictable leaves, cannot pin KV; docs advise starting with lru and changing only against measured hit rate.
does_not_prove: Docs give no benchmark numbers for any policy; no admission control knob in the radix cache itself.
bearing: supports: SGLang is a ready testbed for policy comparison; threatens: claiming SLRU/LFU/TLRU are untested ideas (they are shipped)

title: vLLM docs: Prefix caching design
quote: We only cache full blocks.
proves: vLLM evicts from the head of a free queue (LRU over ref-count-0 blocks); a freed request's blocks enter in reverse order so its last block, which hashes more tokens and is less likely reused, is evicted first; block hash chains parent hash + tokens + extras (LoRA, mm, cache salt); default hash sha256 since v0.11, options sha256_cbor, xxhash, xxhash_cbor.
does_not_prove: No eviction-policy alternative is offered or measured; docs give no hit-rate data.
bearing: supports: vLLM eviction is a fixed LRU with no knob, so any policy change is a code change worth measuring

title: vLLM API docs: CacheConfig
quote: The finest token boundary (in tokens) a prefix-cache hit can land on.
proves: Current vLLM CacheConfig has enable_prefix_caching (default True), prefix_caching_hash_algo (default sha256), block_size (default 16), prefix_match_unit, derived hash_block_size and cache_hit_alignment_tokens (hits can land finer than scheduler block size), prefix_cache_retention_interval for sliding-window/Mamba checkpoints; no field selects an eviction policy.
does_not_prove: Fetched latest docs, not the 0.31.0 pin; whether prefix_match_unit is honored by vllm-metal is unknown; no measured effect of match granularity.
bearing: supports: match-granularity (hash block size vs scheduler block size) tradeoff is a new, unmeasured knob; supports: eviction-policy gap in vLLM

title: Avoiding hash collisions in prefix cache (vLLM forum thread)
quote: Looks like `hashlib.blake2b` + `orjson` is the fastest safe solution.
proves: For 50k tokens (3,125 blocks): Python hash() 0.34 ms vs sha256 2.0 ms without serialization; serialization dominates (sha256+pickle 4.0 ms, +json 10.3 ms); on Apple M2 sha256+pickle 3.58 ms vs hash 0.68 ms; led to PR #15297 switching to sha256.
does_not_prove: Microbenchmarks only; end-to-end results shown only as images; per-request cost relative to prefill on a Mac not measured; xxhash excluded from that test.
bearing: supports: hash cost vs prefill time on slow-prefill devices is a small, measurable question; threatens: claiming hashing is a bottleneck on GPUs

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
quote: Marconi uses the second occurrence to identify the prefix and checkpoint its states.
proves: Hybrid (SSM+attention) models cannot roll back in-place SSM states, so naive prefix caching thrashes; Marconi admits only reuse-likely prefixes (second-occurrence or end-of-round states) and evicts by FLOP savings per byte plus recency; up to 34.4x higher token hit rate vs vLLM+ (avg 4.5x/7.3x/34.4x on LMSys/ShareGPT/SWEBench), 71.1% / 617 ms lower TTFT.
does_not_prove: Hybrid models only; for pure-attention Qwen3 the admission rule is untested; baselines are authors' extended vLLM+/SGLang+.
bearing: supports: admission (second-hit) and FLOP-aware eviction exist only for hybrids; gap: second-hit admission for pure-attention KV at small capacity

title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
quote: the LRU policy identifies the Expresser's KV cache as the eviction candidate since it has not been accessed recently.
proves: In multi-agent workflows LRU evicts the next agent's prefix just before use; KVFlow evicts by steps-to-execution from the workflow graph plus overlapped CPU prefetch; up to 1.83x (single workflow, large prompts) and 2.19x (many concurrent workflows) over SGLang with HiCache.
does_not_prove: No ablation separating eviction from prefetching; needs workflow graph known in advance.
bearing: threatens: workflow-aware eviction; supports: isolating eviction-only effect is an open small experiment

title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
quote: improves the average job completion times by over 8x
proves: Pinning a tool-calling request's KV in GPU memory with a TTL chosen from reload cost and ordering benefit cuts average agent job completion time by over 8x across three agent benchmarks and 8B-355B models.
does_not_prove: TTL tuned for datacenter GPUs; effect when memory is tiny and pins compete with batch is not covered on the page I read.
bearing: threatens: TTL/pinning for agent tool pauses

title: CacheWise: Understanding Workloads and Optimizing KVCache Management for Efficiently Serving LLM Coding Agents
quote: CacheWise reduces KVCache evictions by up to 2-2.6x and improves total agent session completion time by up to 3.5x.
proves: Coding-agent workload study plus predictive eviction using tool-duration estimates cuts evictions 2-2.6x and session completion time up to 3.5x vs conventional serving policies.
does_not_prove: Baselines not named in abstract; workload numbers not in abstract.
bearing: threatens: tool-duration-aware eviction for coding agents

title: PEEK: Predictive Queue-Informed KV Cache Management for LLM Serving
quote: PEEK delivers up to 3.0×/2.6× cache hit, 7.9×/7.1× TTFT, 6.7×/5.5× E2E, and 3.6×/4.5× throughput gains
proves: Eviction that looks at the waiting queue (protect prefixes pending requests need) gives up to 3.0x/2.6x cache hit and 7.9x/7.1x TTFT over best stock SGLang/vLLM baselines.
does_not_prove: Gains are vs stock engines under queueing load; small-batch single-user setting unclear.
bearing: threatens: queue-aware eviction (protect what waiting requests need)

title: Leyline: KV Cache Directives for Agentic Inference
quote: The splice kernel lifts replay cache-hit by +11.2 pp and cuts latency by up to 241 ms.
proves: An interface letting agents issue KV cache directives (e.g. splice, truncation) lifts replay cache hit by 11.2 pp and agentic solve rate by 14.3 pp; per search snippet, it notes a vLLM RFC for pluggable non-LRU eviction ended without an accepted abstraction.
does_not_prove: Pluggable-eviction RFC status is second-hand (from search snippet, not the issue).
bearing: threatens: app-hinted cache directives; supports: vLLM lacks a pluggable eviction API

title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
quote: the cache hit rate ranges from 50% to 99%
proves: RadixAttention: token-level radix tree with LRU leaf eviction; cache-aware scheduling sorts waiting requests by matched prefix length; Theorem 3.1 says DFS order of the radix tree is optimal offline (cache >= max request length); scheduling reaches about 96% of optimal hit rate on average.
does_not_prove: Optimality only for offline batches; benchmarks are structured programs with heavy sharing, not production traces.
bearing: supports: token-level radix vs block hash is a design axis; threatens: cache-aware batch ordering as novel

title: Requests of a Feather Must Flock Together: Batch Size vs. Prefix Homogeneity in LLM Inference
quote: SGLang's LPM and DFS-Weight incur scheduler overhead
proves: SGLang LPM and DFS-Weight batch formation took 46.62 s (31.2%) and 92.15 s (51.8%) of execution time in their test; moderately small prefix-homogeneous batches can beat larger heterogeneous ones; Feather scheduler 2-10x throughput over existing schedulers.
does_not_prove: Datacenter GPU setting; the 128-request FCFS fallback claimed by a search snippet was not found on the page I read.
bearing: threatens: prefix-homogeneous batching; supports: scheduler CPU cost of cache-aware ordering is a real cost on CPU-weak setups

title: Locality-aware Fair Scheduling in LLM Serving (DLPM)
quote: maintaining high throughput (up to 2.87$\times$ higher than VTC)
proves: Longest-prefix-match scheduling can starve clients; deficit-based DLPM keeps locality with fairness: up to 2.87x throughput over VTC and up to 7.18x lower per-client latency than distributed serving SOTA.
does_not_prove: Multi-tenant fairness focus; single-user Mac serving has no tenants.
bearing: threatens: fairness-aware prefix scheduling

title: Preble: Efficient Distributed Prompt Scheduling for LLM Serving
quote: 85% to 97% tokens in a prompt are shared with other prompts.
proves: Workload study of five prompt-heavy workloads: 85-97% of prompt tokens shared, each shared sequence reused by 8.6-126 requests; E2 routing exploits (route to longest-match GPU) when saved recompute exceeds new compute, else explores by load; 1.5x-14.5x avg and 2x-10x p99 latency over SOTA.
does_not_prove: Multi-GPU routing; workloads chosen for sharing (tool use, agents, QA), so share ratio is an upper bound.
bearing: threatens: cache-aware routing; supports: single-node only scheduling/eviction is the relevant scope for a Mac

title: CacheRoute: Planned Prefix-Affinity Routing for Large-Scale LLM Serving
quote: When affinity recovers too little KV work, its residual load skew reduces or erases the improvement.
proves: Planned prefix-affinity routing raises served KV hit rate from 64.1% to 93.2% and gives 176 QPS at 3.5 s p99 on 60 H100 (2.3x best of five baselines); but two 32B workloads are counterexamples where affinity gain vanishes, so authors recommend shadow replay before enabling.
does_not_prove: Cluster routing only.
bearing: negative result: cache affinity can lose when reusable work is small; threatens: cache-aware routing as novel

title: qwen-bailian-usagetraces-anon (GitHub)
quote: a two-hour sampled anonymized KVCache trace of requests sent to a single Qwen model serving cluster
proves: Public trace with chat_id, parent_chat_id, timestamp, input/output length, type, turn, and hash_ids (salted SipHash-2-4 over 16-token blocks, chat template already applied); files for To-C chat, To-B API, thinking, coder.
does_not_prove: Only 2 hours; hash block 16 fixes the finest match granularity you can replay; no token content.
bearing: supports: replayable reuse trace at vLLM's default block size, usable for eviction/admission simulation on a Mac

title: Mooncake FAST25 trace release
quote: Identical hash IDs indicate reusable prefix KV cache blocks.
proves: Released Kimi traces: conversation (12,031 req), toolagent (23,608 req), synthetic (3,993 req); fields timestamp, input_length, output_length, hash_ids; block size 512 tokens; raw text excluded.
does_not_prove: 512-token blocks are too coarse to study fine match granularity or 16-token block eviction; replay lengths sized for large GPUs.
bearing: supports: agent-vs-chat reuse comparisons in simulation; limits: granularity studies

title: BurstGPT (GitHub repo)
quote: conversation ID, only conversation mode have this
proves: 10.31M Azure OpenAI requests over 213 days with Timestamp, Session ID, Model, request/response tokens, log type; Session ID allows approximate multi-turn grouping.
does_not_prove: No prompt hashes or text, so actual prefix overlap cannot be measured.
bearing: limits: cannot drive prefix-reuse studies beyond session-level approximations

title: Azure LLM inference trace 2023
quote: Due to customer privacy requirements (e.g., GDPR), we do not have visibility into the content of the prompts.
proves: Fields are only TIMESTAMP, ContextTokens, GeneratedTokens.
does_not_prove: No session, prefix, or hash data; useless for reuse studies except arrival/length shape.
bearing: limits: Azure trace cannot test prefix policies

title: Cost-Efficient Large Language Model Serving for Multi-turn Conversations with CachedAttention
quote: decreases the time to the first token (TTFT) by up to 87%
proves: Keeping multi-turn KV in a hierarchical store with layer-wise preload, async save, and scheduler-aware fetch/eviction cuts TTFT up to 87%, raises prefill throughput up to 7.8x, cuts cost up to 70%.
does_not_prove: No eviction-policy-only numbers in abstract; assumes host DRAM/SSD tiers separate from GPU memory.
bearing: threatens: multi-turn KV retention across tiers; note: unified memory removes the GPU/host tier split this assumes

title: Stateful Large Language Model Serving with Pensieve
quote: Pensieve's multi-tier caching strategy can utilize both GPU and CPU memory.
proves: Multi-turn conversation state cached across GPU and CPU memory avoids reprocessing history; 1.14-3.0x throughput of vLLM and TensorRT-LLM.
does_not_prove: Eviction cost details not in abstract.
bearing: threatens: multi-turn conversation cache as novel

title: Building py-kvcache: A Performance Characterization of External KV Caching for vLLM with NVMe SSDs
quote: External KV caching should therefore be treated as a setup specific admission decision.
proves: For short prefixes or fast GPUs recomputation can beat loading from external cache; on H100 the average Bailian-trace request is below break-even and GPU memory alone holds enough prefixes; py-kvcache disk load 2.0x faster than LMCache at 80k tokens.
does_not_prove: H100 + NVMe; break-even on a slow-prefill Apple GPU with fast SSD would differ and is unmeasured.
bearing: supports: admission by break-even (prefill cost vs load cost) is device-specific and open for Apple silicon

title: Randomization Boosts KV Caching, Learning Balances Query Load: A Joint Perspective
quote: improvements of up to 6.92×in cache hit rate, 11.96× reduction in latency
proves: Joint randomized KV eviction plus learned load balancing across workers gives up to 6.92x cache hit and 11.96x latency over SOTA on 4 benchmarks and 3 prefix-sharing settings; argues LRU struggles under dynamic online arrivals.
does_not_prove: Multi-worker routing setting; gains vs chosen SOTA, not plain LRU in isolation.
bearing: threatens: randomized eviction as novel

title: The Early Bird Catches the Leak: Unveiling Timing Side Channels in LLM Serving Systems
quote: the accuracy of detecting per-token cache hits or misses in the KV cache is 99%
proves: Prefix-cache hits are detectable by timing (99% per-token), enabling prompt recovery (89.0%); mitigation of sharing only in units of k tokens drops recovery from 91.5% (k=1) to 49.0% (k=4) and raises query cost.
does_not_prove: Security, not performance; does not measure the hit-rate cost of coarser sharing units.
bearing: supports: match-granularity has a security side; open: hit-rate cost of coarse match units

title: SGLang docs: HiCache system design
quote: Data is written back only after the access frequency exceeds a threshold.
proves: SGLang HiCache exposes tier admission via --hicache-write-policy: write_through (default), write_through_selective (hot data only), write_back (on eviction); L3 prefetch only above 256 tokens by default.
does_not_prove: No measurements of the write policies on the page.
bearing: supports: admission knobs exist in SGLang tiers but are unmeasured; no equivalent for the GPU tier

title: SGLang router: cache-aware routing
proves: Per search snippet: router keeps an approximate per-worker radix tree of raw text characters, routes to longest match above cache_threshold, falls back to shortest queue when load imbalance exceeds balance_abs/rel thresholds.
does_not_prove: Fetch failed (404 after redirect); details from search snippets only.
bearing: threatens: approximate cache-aware routing

title: llm-d: Precise prefix cache aware routing
proves: Per search snippet: vLLM/SGLang/TRT-LLM publish KV block events over ZMQ; router indexes by block hash and scores pods by resident prefix fraction; secondary blogs claim up to 57x response time and up to 108% throughput.
does_not_prove: Not opened; benchmark numbers only from secondary blogs.
bearing: threatens: event-driven cache-aware routing
